# Invariants (A-D)

<!-- generated by scripts/verify_docs.py --write-nav; do not hand-edit -->

> Code is the source of truth. This file is a map; when it and the code disagree, the code wins.

Every invariant is defined in exactly one file and referenced by id elsewhere.

The index is sharded by family letter: see also [`doctrine/invariants-e.md`](invariants-e.md), [`doctrine/invariants-f-m.md`](invariants-f-m.md), [`doctrine/invariants-n-pk.md`](invariants-n-pk.md), [`doctrine/invariants-pl-r.md`](invariants-pl-r.md), [`doctrine/invariants-s.md`](invariants-s.md), [`doctrine/invariants-t-z.md`](invariants-t-z.md).

| Id | Statement | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| `INV-AGENT-001` | A role claimed by both a resident and a specialist is refused at boot, when the role registry is built. | [`architecture/agent-taxonomy.md`](../architecture/agent-taxonomy.md) |
| `INV-AGENT-002` | For residents and specialists, `_check_file_set` refuses a missing required file, a forbidden file, or an unrecognised one. | [`architecture/agent-taxonomy.md`](../architecture/agent-taxonomy.md) |
| `INV-AGENT-003` | Specialist loading is isolated per agent and boot-non-fatal; resident loading is not. | [`architecture/agent-taxonomy.md`](../architecture/agent-taxonomy.md) |
| `INV-AGENT-004` | The registry performs no filesystem access; it is an index built from already-loaded configuration. | [`architecture/agent-taxonomy.md`](../architecture/agent-taxonomy.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-001` | A job engagement's next batch is started only while the record is live, the ended turn was not cut off, no turn is queued and no turn delivery is in progress; the previous batch is judged, the batch number chosen and the batch cap checked in the same synchronous step that admits it, and that batch is counted only once the hand-off has been accepted — a refused hand-off leaves every counter untouched. | [`architecture/background-jobs.md`](../architecture/background-jobs.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-002` | A job fails through the engagement finalize funnel, with the reason and its last reported progress, when three consecutive batches report no progress or end without reporting, when a batch would exceed its declared batch cap, when a batch's delivery raises, or when a batch is cut off before finishing — and a clearance downgrade never cuts a running batch. | [`architecture/background-jobs.md`](../architecture/background-jobs.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-003` | A job that is not progressing is continued by the periodic job sweep — no turn queued, no delivery owner live, no launch enrolled, and no advance for the stall window — and the sweep's own decision to end a job rests only on three of its continuations having been refused, never on a reading of the record's state; a continuation it attempts may still end the job through the paths that own that outcome (an engagement with no session to resume, the batch cap, the no-progress guard), and a hand-off refused because Casa is stopping is not a failed continuation and leaves the record live for boot. | [`architecture/background-jobs.md`](../architecture/background-jobs.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-004` | A resident-hosted job's session is offered exactly its declaring plugin's tools, `Skill`, `ToolSearch` and the two job tools — never a delegation, messaging, memory or question tool, and never the resident's own settings, prompt or plugins. | [`architecture/background-jobs.md`](../architecture/background-jobs.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-005` | Every turn of a fresh job after its launch is preceded, under the turn lock, by a conversation reset that is confirmed before the turn is accepted, and begins with the job brief built only from the record's task, its clearance-governed launch context, and Casa's record of who started it; a resume-mode job and every non-job engagement are unchanged. | [`architecture/background-job-fresh-sessions.md`](../architecture/background-job-fresh-sessions.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-006` | At most one job per plugin manifest name is live or starting, whichever host kind runs it and whatever the record's shape: `start_job` refuses with `job_busy` while a job record whose qualified job name carries the requested job's manifest name is live or its strict terminal write is still pending, or while another start of that manifest name is inside its pre-record window. | [`architecture/background-job-occupancy.md`](../architecture/background-job-occupancy.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-007` | A completion a fresh job's worker requested and the completion gate refused for unread input is recorded on the job and named in every later brief until the record is terminal — without its text once the clearance was lowered; while it is recorded, a held ingress reservation holds the next batch back, and a job that reaches its batch cap or the no-progress guard is spared one batch, once per job. | [`architecture/background-job-fresh-sessions.md`](../architecture/background-job-fresh-sessions.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-008` | A specialist's `start_job` starts only a job declared by a plugin assigned to that specialist and loadable when it is called, hosted by that specialist; it is offered only to a desk or delegated turn whose session loads a job-declaring plugin (a tap's pin refuses it, a job or engagement session never holds it), and the job launches with the calling turn's origin — its clearance, chat and resident — at depth 1, under every launch gate a resident's start of that job applies except the delegation ACL and the depth cap. | [`architecture/specialist-job-start.md`](../architecture/specialist-job-start.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-009` | The resident's `<jobs>` listing marks a job as a delegate's own, to be started through a sync text delegation to that delegate, only when that delegate's own `start_job` would accept it at render time; the assistant's served text projection tells it to delegate such a job and that a delegation runs it, and its voice projection that no job starts on a call; it keeps `start_job` for every job it lists; and a specialist's own start returns no engagement or topic id, while the resident's results still carry them. | [`architecture/specialist-job-start.md`](../architecture/specialist-job-start.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-010` | A run of a job declaring `quietWhenScheduled` that the scheduler started opens no topic and posts nothing to Telegram except its plugin's delivered slots and Casa's tellings that need the operator — an approval challenge, a cancelled or failed end; a completed end is told to no one and arms no end notification; every other run, and every job without the option, opens its topic and is told as before. | [`architecture/background-job-quiet-runs.md`](../architecture/background-job-quiet-runs.md) |
| `INV-BRW-001` | Root bootstrap removes the Supervisor token from the s6 container environment on every start, also when bootstrap fails, and writes it to no file or log. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-002` | At most one run is between `starting` and `finishing`; the FIFO lease is taken in one immediate transaction. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-003` | The retention sweep unlinks only paths whose parent directory resolves inside the artifacts directory, and removes a symlink itself, never its target. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-004` | Every `/v1` route requires `Authorization: Bearer <pairing secret>`, except `POST /v1/pair/claim` while the pairing window is open, and every `POST` requires `X-Casa-Browser-Protocol: 1`; both are checked before the route acts. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-005` | A run is queued only when the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the received members other than `admission` equals the admitted digest. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-006` | Exactly one claim inside an armed two-minute window receives the secret, and arming revokes the previous secret and everything issued under it. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-012` | The broker listener admits a request only to a listed 1Password host on port 443 whose `CONNECT` host, TLS server name and `Host` header are the same host. | [`reference/casa-browser-runtime.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runtime.md) |
| `INV-BRW-013` | Chrome starts only as the browser user, only from the launcher, only for a controller-user caller, only with the network floor installed, and always with the Chromium sandbox and a pipe as its only debugging channel. | [`reference/casa-browser-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-016` | A stored file is complete and within its bound; a refused, failed or cancelled transfer leaves no file and no record. | [`reference/casa-browser-files.md`](../reference/casa-browser-files.md) |
| `INV-BRW-019` | No code path in the broker removes a vault item: the broker package uses only the vault facade's read, create and update calls of the 1Password SDK, has no removal, archive or password-generation call and no dynamic attribute access, and forgetting a site changes only the broker's registry. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-022` | A credential is set only on the validated element of a frame whose origin is one of the active site's registered login origins, in the page and generation the driver session is bound to; it never travels as keyboard input. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-023` | While a credential window is open, a proxy event carries only fixed-vocabulary members — its origin only when the run registered it (or it is a fixed extension, broker or infrastructure host), the policy's enums, a normalised method, and keyed binding tags or a callback reference — never request identity, path, query, header or body bytes. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-024` | A session's policy is installed only after the launcher confirmed that no Chrome of the browser user runs; a run takes its intended terminal state, and the next queued run starts, only after its four holds are released — that proof, the proxy's acknowledged revoke of its policy, no driver session left and (an account run) the broker's acknowledged `end_run` — and a run whose release is unconfirmed ends `interrupted`, saying so, while no queued run starts until the release is confirmed. | [`reference/casa-browser-runs.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runs.md) |
| `INV-BRW-025` | A run is never resumed or reinstalled after a restart: a proxy restart, a controller restart and every dependency failure interrupt it, and every install names the proxy start it expects, which a restarted proxy refuses. | [`reference/casa-browser-runs.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runs.md) |
| `INV-BRW-027` | Every driver session the controller opens is closed on every path, and a login or assist live view on an account session exposes the operator's input only after the broker acknowledged its capture (a public-session assist view runs no capture). | [`reference/casa-browser-runs.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runs.md) |
| `INV-BRW-028` | Only a page of the run's public session, `https` and at most 800 bytes, gets a source id, and its address leaves the app only through the trusted sources route. | [`reference/casa-browser-runs.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runs.md) |
| `INV-BRW-030` | Only Home Assistant's ingress peer reaches the UI — nginx admits that one address and the UI requires a well-formed `X-Ingress-Path` — and every mutation needs a single-use nonce issued for its own path from a same-origin page. | [`reference/casa-browser-ingress.md`](../reference/casa-browser-ingress.md) |
| `INV-BRW-031` | No operator input reaches Chrome before the view's session exists, which is only after the run entered `live` and, on an account session, its manual lease and (login/assist) the broker's capture acknowledgement, nor after any end of the view, which takes effect before anything else is awaited and lets only the operation in flight finish; a page that is no longer the current viewer gets no socket and no input. | [`reference/casa-browser-ingress.md`](../reference/casa-browser-ingress.md) |
| `INV-BRW-032` | A live view returns its run to `running` only after its sockets are closed and every window it resized is back to its earlier bounds, verified with the screen at 1920×1080; a restore that cannot be verified interrupts the run. | [`reference/casa-browser-ingress.md`](../reference/casa-browser-ingress.md) |
| `INV-BRW-034` | A provider binding is shown as bound only when it was learned under the proxy's current binding key; one learned under another key (an HA restore makes a new one) or under no recorded key is shown as needing a live login, and forgetting the site clears it. | [`reference/casa-browser-ingress.md`](../reference/casa-browser-ingress.md) |
| `INV-BRW-036` | An in-scope action runs only after a verdict whose digest is its own frozen packet's; no verdict, a verdict outside the reply bounds, another digest or a stale id runs nothing. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
| `INV-BRW-037` | A tap executes the frozen operation at most once, and only after a `same` re-judgement and a final read identical to the reading it judged. | [`reference/casa-browser-approvals.md`](../reference/casa-browser-approvals.md) |
| `INV-BRW-038` | A question offers a confirm button only when the check stated its facts (`text_incomplete` false) and, for a money question, the app holds a faithful question screenshot. | [`reference/casa-browser-approvals.md`](../reference/casa-browser-approvals.md) |
| `INV-BRW-039` | A judged press happens only after the target-fact re-read and the hit test pass, immediately before `mouse.down()`; a failure presses nothing. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
| `INV-BRW-040` | In an account session the policy admits a top-level document — or a request whose class the browser did not state — only on the active site's origins and login origins, on a run site's origins or login origins during a live view's manual lease, or as the exact recorded provider binding during the run's login lease. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-041` | In every session, and for every download hop, a request to an address the floor refuses is refused, Chrome's own background sends to its background hosts are refused, and a fixed exception — an infrastructure rule or the provider binding — admits a request only within its declared shape. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-042` | On the browser and download listeners no byte reaches an upstream for a request the current policy refuses — an account session's off-site top-level document included, while its pages' other requests reach any floor-checked origin — the proxy dials only an address the floor checked for that host (never a name resolved outside a decision), and once a policy change is acknowledged no request or WebSocket frame admitted under the earlier policy is sent, except that `end_login` and `end_manual` leave in flight what the policy after them admits when no lease has admitted anything the policy without leases refuses since the last close of every connection, and an `install` that only adds provider bindings leaves everything in flight. | [`reference/casa-browser-runtime.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runtime.md) |
| `INV-BRW-043` | An observation or a screenshot is produced only when the page-view gate admits the page's full current address as the session's own — in an account session, the site's origins or login origins; in the public session, an address the floor admits — before and after it is read, and an observation carries no address beyond an origin, no attribute, no selector and no value of a field the one secret rule recognises — a password, one-time-code or payment-card field, as the field is when it is read — each field whose value it shows being asked that rule again right after the reading. | [`reference/casa-browser-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-044` | In an account run a navigation to an address off the run's account sites is sent only from the public session, after the account browser closed; a top-level navigation the run's leases-free policy refuses is never sent and is answered `blocked`; and the model never types into a password field. | [`reference/casa-browser-runs.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runs.md) |
| `INV-BRW-045` | A download hop the run's policy refuses as a download hop is never sent; a hop it admits is decided again by the enforcing proxy on its download listener, which alone admits it to the upstream, and an account cookie is attached only to a hop whose origin is the link's page's or the active account site's. | [`reference/casa-browser-files.md`](../reference/casa-browser-files.md) |
| `INV-BRW-046` | A public link download whose detected type is outside the document set is recorded only when a go verdict or an executed confirmation for its own pending judgement keeps it, and at any other end of that judgement its bytes are deleted. | [`reference/casa-browser-files.md`](../reference/casa-browser-files.md) |
| `INV-BRW-047` | Each service user can open only its one permitted route — the browser user the proxy's browser listener, the controller user the proxy's download listener, the broker user the proxy's broker listener, the proxy user public TCP and the configured resolver, the VNC user none, the ingress user only replies on its port — and no service starts unless root init installed that floor. | [`reference/casa-browser-runtime.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runtime.md) |
| `INV-BRW-048` | A live-view credential is written only from the capture's last attempt that the check judged `signed_in`, that did not fail, with no password typing after it, ending on one of the site's origins; it overwrites a linked item only when that item is `unverified` or its own password was rejected in this run, and never writes equal values. | [`reference/casa-browser-signin.md`](../reference/casa-browser-signin.md) |
| `INV-BRW-049` | The broker never changes a credential on its own: a page offering a new-password field during a login ends that login for the live view before anything is filled, and a captured value reaches the vault only through a live-view sign-in the check judged signed in (INV-BRW-048). | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-050` | Forgetting a site's login removes only its item link: the site stays registered with its login origins, no vault call is made, and its next login asks the operator again. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-051` | A site's sign-in code is filled only into the one code field of the very document that reported `needs_code` (the same page generation and the mark the report set in that document, on a login origin, with exactly that field and a submit), once per report, through a fresh login driver session closed on every path; it never appears in a broker or API reply, an error, the run's events, the broker's journal or registry, the app's records, or a log line. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
| `INV-BRW-052` | A line break an agent types reaches only a real `<textarea>`, only after a verdict on the packet holding the whole text, never with Enter after it, and only as inserted text, never as a key. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
| `INV-BRW-053` | A site is registered from a sign-in card only by the operator's Yes on that card, for exactly the origin the card showed (read from the browser, never from the model), and a card never signs in to a registered site that reaches more than that origin. | [`reference/casa-browser-signin.md`](../reference/casa-browser-signin.md) |
| `INV-BRW-054` | Only `confirm` can execute a question's frozen operation: `not_now` declines and an extra option answers, neither pressing anything, and a tap on a question that is no longer current (another revision or digest, lapsed, expired) executes nothing. | [`reference/casa-browser-approvals.md`](../reference/casa-browser-approvals.md) |
| `INV-BRW-055` | What the probe reads goes only to the current viewer — never to a log, a model or any other surface; it holds a password field's length, never its value. | [`reference/casa-browser-ingress.md`](../reference/casa-browser-ingress.md) |
| `INV-BRW-056` | An automatic sign-in whose page changed under a step reads the page again from settling before any further value is set, and only while every frame holding one of the step's live handles has kept, throughout, the address origin it had when the handle was issued and stayed attached (otherwise it refuses); it reports `logged_in` only after a submit of its own — a read with no fields after the step's fields were found is `page_unsettled`, and a sign-in that filled nothing and found no form is `no_form`. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-057` | The 1Password guest's email, Secret Key and password are set only into the main frame of the guest session's own tab, and only while that document is exactly `https://my.1password.<region>/signin` (sign-in) or the extension's popup page (unlock), checked in the same evaluation that sets the value. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-058` | An automatic sign-in answers a passkey prompt only through 1Password's notification frame of the login page itself, on a login origin, when the prompt offers exactly the site's linked item (its username, and its title, which names no other login in the vault once trimmed), at most once per run and site, and a sign-in that answered it — continued with a code or not — claims nothing (`no_form`). | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-059` | Off the start page, Casa Browser fills or presses nothing of a sign-in without a `sign_in` verdict on that page, only fields of the judged reading (a field the page does not mark only as the verdict mapped it, a password only into a password field), and only while the documents, destinations, labels and text it judged are unchanged and no step came between; a look sends the password once, answers only its judged page's passkey, and signs in again only after a sign-in of the run that worked. | [`reference/casa-browser-signin.md`](../reference/casa-browser-signin.md) |
| `INV-BRW-060` | An automatic sign-in sends the password at most once per sign-in, and never while a shown, editable, empty box of its form stays unfilled: the read and the click's own evaluation both check it, and a form that asks again goes to the live view. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-CB-001` | The callback route serves only names present in the consented overlay; a request for any other name performs no spool mutation. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-002` | A pending state is consumed at most once — the claim-by-rename is the consumption point — and a replayed redirect never rewrites or duplicates a result. | [`architecture/callback-delivery.md`](../architecture/callback-delivery.md) |
| `INV-CB-003` | A callback ack binds `(plugin, effective, declaration_digest)`; the ack store fails closed whole-store on any malformed or key-mismatched record; and plugin removal revokes its acks and unroutes. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-004` | Casa relays the query opaquely — the raw query string plus an ordered list of decoded key/value pairs — and interprets only `state`; no provider-specific parsing lives in core. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-005` | For a syntactically-accepted GET that reaches the app, success and every refusal cause yield the same status, headers and redirect target, at any traffic level — there is no throttle response. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-006` | The callback query string never reaches the app access logger, the app handler and exception logs, or the in-container nginx access logs; an unrouted name logs a fixed sentinel. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-007` | Every minted state a casa pass observes ends in exactly one of two ways — a consumer ack, or one terminal outcome written durably before the flow's last credential-bearing artifact is deleted and retained until that ack or the attempt retention bound. | [`architecture/callback-delivery.md`](../architecture/callback-delivery.md) |
| `INV-CB-008` | The delivery nudge re-fires on a durable schedule until receipt — the attempt leaving `result_ready` — or until the budget of six accepted dispatches is spent, whichever comes first, and a spent budget raises exactly one operator note. | [`architecture/callback-delivery.md`](../architecture/callback-delivery.md) |
| `INV-CB-009` | The consumer's `meta` is size-capped, stored and echoed value-preserving, never interpreted, and never reaches a log surface. | [`architecture/callback-delivery.md`](../architecture/callback-delivery.md) |
| `INV-CB-010` | A callback reconcile whose caller is cancelled holds the reconcile lock until the marker and ack writes it has already handed to a worker thread have settled, however many cancellations arrive; and a pass that had already published its overlay delivers one setup-worker kick after those writes settle and before the cancellation propagates. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-011` | An operator note the worker attempts while the Telegram channel is not ready, before the channels have finished starting, is logged at INFO without a traceback, and an owed exhaustion or removal note stays owed; every other failed note keeps an ERROR with its traceback. | [`architecture/callback-delivery.md`](../architecture/callback-delivery.md) |
| `INV-CFG-001` | Exactly seven reload scopes exist, and none of them rereads the app manifest options. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-002` | A full reload excludes every other dispatched reload for its duration. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-003` | A live resident identity change is restart-only: an in-process reload neither hot-swaps the resident nor promotes its staged binding on disk before the restart that activates it. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-004` | Only an explicit whitelist of the config tree is version-controlled. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-005` | Reconciliation of the config tree is never boot-fatal. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-006` | In a file reconciled per entry, an entry whose name the image has never shipped is preserved, except when the image ships that name for the first time. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-007` | Reconciliation never writes a config file that fails its schema. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-008` | Entry-level reconciliation only ever writes a `schema_version` that already appears among its input documents; it never synthesizes or migrates one. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-009` | A `${VAR}` placeholder is resolved once its scalar is being built, so a variable's contents are never lexed as part of the document, and a quoted placeholder's value reaches its field unaltered. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-010` | An in-process rewrite of a config file re-emits a scalar the source declared as text and whose whole value is a `${VAR}` placeholder still declared as text, so the rewrite changes neither what that scalar means nor whether the refusal above applies to the file afterwards. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-011` | A reload scope whose handler takes the plugin-mutation lock acquires that lock at the entry point, before the reload read/write lock — never underneath it. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-012` | A reload that reads a specialist's `enabled: false` constructs and registers nothing for it and retires none of its Casa-minted secret slots; and for each of — its runtime agent, its bus queue, its scheduled jobs and webhook routes, its agent-registry entry, its delegation-map entry — the reload either removes it or names the step that failed in its report or its error; whichever scope read the file. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-013` | A specialist read as disabled — by the reload scope that retires it, by an `agents` sweep whether or not it has a runtime Agent, or at boot after the channels start and before background jobs resume — has a close attempted through the terminal funnel, as a named retirement step, for each of its open conversations; a close that fails leaves that conversation open, is told to the operator, is named in the reload's report (at boot, in the log) and is retried by the next `agents` sweep that still reads the specialist disabled; a specialist that failed to load has nothing closed. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-014` | A configurator run, from any origin, takes the one process-wide configurator lease before its ceiling clock starts and before anything of the run starts, waiting up to `LEASE_WAIT_S` for the holder, for running plugin erasures and for specialist-bundle transactions still running after their handler was cancelled; a run that cannot take it by then is refused with the busy text naming the holder's task and nothing of it runs; the lease is released when the run ends, and a failure before the run starts releases it at once. | [`architecture/configurator.md`](../architecture/configurator.md) |
| `INV-CFG-015` | A configurator run that ends while Casa is stopping, whether cancelled or returning after it swallowed the cancellation, leaves its lease record on disk; the next boot removes that record and, once the channels are up, tells the operator once which task was interrupted, unless the job registry's restart recovery announces the same delegation; nothing of the run is replayed. | [`architecture/configurator.md`](../architecture/configurator.md) |
| `INV-CFG-016` | A `casa_restart_supervised` call inside a delegated run restarts nothing: it records the need and returns `deferred`; after that run's answer Casa posts one Restart now button, spent on its first tap, which asks the Supervisor for the restart, and a button that expires is edited to say so. | [`architecture/configurator.md`](../architecture/configurator.md) |
| `INV-CFG-017` | `config_git_commit`, `casa_reload`, `casa_restart_supervised`, `config_trigger_upsert`, `config_trigger_delete` and `casa_reload_triggers` authorise on the executing role — the `execution_role` Casa stamps on a delegated run's or desk turn's origin, else a bound engagement's role, else the origin's role — and refuse every role but the configurator with `not_authorized`. | [`architecture/configurator.md`](../architecture/configurator.md) |
| `INV-CFG-018` | While a configurator run holds the lease, the operator DM neither names nor marks the plugin-health rows whose reason is an install phase (consent pending, a setup-provided value unwired, setup pending, not loaded yet, target pending) of the plugins that run is installing; every other row is sent as before; and when the lease is released in this process after such a run, a notify pass runs that can name those rows. | [`architecture/configurator.md`](../architecture/configurator.md) |
| `INV-CONC-001` | The bus dequeues per role in priority order and spawns one task per message; it never serializes handler execution. | [`architecture/concurrency-model.md`](../architecture/concurrency-model.md) |
| `INV-CONC-002` | A role has at most one live consumer task, and re-registration replaces the handler while preserving the queue. | [`architecture/concurrency-model.md`](../architecture/concurrency-model.md) |
| `INV-CONC-003` | Turns sharing a session key serialize under the pool entry's lock, decision through publication; distinct keys are concurrent. | [`architecture/concurrency-model.md`](../architecture/concurrency-model.md) |
| `INV-CONC-004` | Every turn serializes under one per-session-key write gate, held from the resume decision through the session-id publish, regardless of which turn path it takes. | [`architecture/concurrency-model.md`](../architecture/concurrency-model.md) |
| `INV-CONC-006` | The graceful stop's completion record carries the number of turns the bus had dispatched and had not finished at the instant it was written, together with the reason they were left — that they are neither awaited nor cancelled — and exactly one record in a stop carries that count. | [`architecture/concurrency-model.md`](../architecture/concurrency-model.md) |
| `INV-DESK-002` | A desk turn's reply reaches the operator only as an admitted, labelled, paginated post of the specialist's own completed and bounded text — of a run that ended with a protected call waiting on the operator's approval, only the text written before that call; of a reply whose last text-bearing message is only `<silent/>` after earlier text, nothing after a proven outcome with no approval pending, else the earlier messages without it; and never with a `<silent/>` marker at the start or end of its words — whose messages join the post map; a turn that produces no proven operator-visible outcome, or whose reply is not proven, ends in one labelled Casa notice; the chat's resident learns of the turn only through a body-free line at its next turn, and no resident model turn is spent on it. | [`architecture/specialist-desk-reply.md`](../architecture/specialist-desk-reply.md) |
| `INV-DESK-003` | A desk's log holds at most twelve bounded exchanges, in arrival order, shared by swipe-replies and the resident's delegations to that specialist from that chat from the first of them — every completed desk turn an exchange — and is empty on the first use after the idle bound or a restart; every use of a desk — a swipe-reply, a continuation, a sync, degraded or async delegation — runs alone under its lock from the log read to the exchange's commit, in arrival order, and no later use starts a run while an earlier use's run, cut off at the ceiling or by a cancellation, is still unwinding — the desk refuses it until that run has ended. | [`architecture/specialist-desk.md`](../architecture/specialist-desk.md) |
| `INV-DESK-004` | A Telegram DM text message that replies to another message and that the desk does not take reaches the chat's resident with its text unchanged and one Casa-composed note on the reserved `_reply_note` context key, naming who posted the quoted message — decided from Casa's post map and Telegram's sender ids, never from text — when, and what it read, clipped to 600 characters. | [`architecture/specialist-desk.md`](../architecture/specialist-desk.md) |
| `INV-DESK-005` | An operator's Telegram message that quotes a message Casa posted for an agent that holds a desk (a specialist or the configurator) in that chat, for that operator, and still retained in its post map, reaches that agent as one desk turn carrying the operator's exact words — never a resident turn — when it is one the chat's resident may delegate to; every other message, quoting or not, takes the resident's path. | [`architecture/specialist-desk.md`](../architecture/specialist-desk.md) |
| `INV-DOC-001` | Every document repeats the code-wins line verbatim at the top, under front matter carrying `last_reviewed`. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-002` | An architecture document follows one section order — Scope, Mental model, Contracts & invariants, Failure behavior, Extension points, Source & test map — so an agent can skim positionally; documents in the other directories keep the code-wins line and the source map but shape their own sections. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-003` | A document describes the present system — no changelog voice, no "as of version X", no discrepancy log, no TODOs, no open questions; past tense may explain a mechanism, never track the document's own history. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-004` | A cross-cutting rule is defined exactly once, as `**INV-AREA-NNN**: <single-line statement>`, and referenced by id rather than restated. Issue ids sparingly — an id per local rule is bureaucracy, and the define-once check makes over-issuing visibly expensive; nothing mechanical enforces a minimum reference count. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-005` | Anchors are typed symbols (`path/to/file.py::Class.method`, `config.yaml::schema.key`, `tests/test_x.py::test_name`) or tracked bare paths; never `file:line`, which rots silently on the next edit. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-007` | Growth splits, it never appends: the change that crosses the size ceiling lands visibly, the next change touching the over-ceiling document — its file or its manifest row — must split it first, a new path may not be born over the ceiling, and the ceiling is not raised; nothing shards on its own. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-008` | A `Docs-impact:` waiver is checked against the diff it ships with — the waived documents are exactly the documents the change impacts and does not update, no document is waived twice, the reserved token `none` asserts that set is empty, only the tip commit may carry a waiver line, a subject line is never one, and every tip carries a line; whether a waiver's reason is true remains a review question. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-009` | An invariant id cited in a comment or a docstring of a tracked Python file outside `docs/`, in a family the corpus defines, must be an id the corpus defines. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-010` | Generated navigation is rendered only from a manifest that loads — when the root manifest or any `manifest.d/` shard fails to load, the corpus check and `--write-nav` report the source and the error, write no generated artifact, and do not report the navigation as stale. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
